messages:
Tara: ACME infra reported a sudden latency + 502 spike for EU users starting ~03:40 UTC. They say requests are landing in us-central instead of eu-west and auth fails. Ticket INC-7531.
Mike: Can you paste a sample request/response header? :eyes:
Tara: from their logs: 
```
GET /v1/chat
Host: api.redwood.com
X-Client-Region: eu-west
X-Forwarded-For: 78.33.21.10
X-Redwood-Region: us-central
Status: 502
Latency: 1.2s
```
They also included resolver traces showing DNS resolved to an anycast IP that routes to our US edge.
Jin: Are they using a corporate resolver or consumer ISPs? Any EDNS/ClientSubnet info?
Tara: They say corporate proxy + internal resolvers. Example dig from one of their EU nodes: `dig +short @10.0.0.5 api.redwood.com` -> 104.21.55.12 (our anycast IP). TTL returned = 3600.
Anya: TTL=3600 is expected, but resolver cache might be sticky to an old GeoIP mapping. Which GeoIP DB version did the edge use when traffic hit us?
SRE_Tim: Pulling ingress logs now. I see a batch of EU source IPs (78.33.x.x) hitting us-central at 03:39:42 UTC, GeoIP DB reported version `2026-03-01`. Latest deployed DB is `2026-03-15` after last week's refresh. :grimacing:
Mike: That mismatch explains wrong-region routing if our anycast selection used the old DB. Why didn't the DB auto-refresh on those nodes?
Jin: We had a staggered GeoIP roll last week; a subset of edge pods missed restart due to a flaky configmap mount. Nodes that missed reboot remained on 03-01.
Tara: ACME says impact started after March-12 deploy window. They escalated because they saw auth token validation errors that correlated with cross-region hops.
Anya: Auth errors make sense: token issuer validation short-circuited with region-specific signing keys when routed to wrong >region. Also TTL=3600 means resolver caches can keep bad mapping for an hour.
Mike: Immediate mitigations: 1) Force GeoIP DB reload on all edge nodes, 2) Push a TTL override to reduce to 60s for api.redwood.com via our DNS provider (short-term), 3) Instruct ACME to flush corporate resolver cache or enable EDNS-client-subnet.
Jin: I'm running `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/edge-geodb` now. Also triggering a GeoIP checksum scan across edges. Deploy-bot: rollout started on 12 nodes.
Tara: I asked ACME for a traceroute and one full sample curl with headers. They sent this: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
< HTTP/2 502
< x-redwood-region: us-central
< x-edge-geodb-version: 2026-03-01
```
SRE_Tim: Confirmed. I also see resolver telemetry showing some resolvers returning stale NS answers due to intermediate ISP caches. There were multiple resolver chains where edns-client-subnet was stripped.
Anya: Short-term patch: enable per-request region hint fallback — if X-Client-Region != X-Redwood-Region, prefer regional backends rather than defaulting to the anycast route. I'll prepare a canary.
Mike: Ops action list in thread: 
- Jin: force GeoIP reload & verify checksums (in progress)
- Anya: canary for region-hint fallback + telemetry (ETA 2h)
- Tara: coordinate with ACME on resolver flush steps + confirm impact window
- SRE_Tim: update runbook with stale-geoip detection and alert thresholds
Tara: ACME confirmed that after we restarted edge nodes they saw immediate improvement for ~30% of requests, still seeing some clients hitting US due to ISP caches.
Jin: We pushed GeoIP v2026-03-15 to all edges and restarted the remaining 6 nodes. All edges now report `x-edge-geodb-version: 2026-03-15` in 200 responses. :white_check_mark:
Mike: I lowered the authoritative TTL to 60s for api.redwood.com and requested DNS provider purge. That should limit cache duration for any future mismatches. Provider confirms purge completed.
Tara: ACME ran a couple of validation runs and reports latency back to normal and auth errors gone. They asked for a postmortem and a path to avoid recurrence.
Anya: Postmortem action items: automated GeoIP rollout with pre/post checksums, ensure configmap mount reliability, alert when node geodb version != control-plane version, and implement region-hint fallback canary.
SRE_Tim: Logging note: added a tooltip metric `edge.geodb.version_mismatch` and a paging rule if >5% of requests in 5m have mismatch.
Tara: I'll update INC-7531 with timeline and assign PM/Eng owners. Thanks team. :clap:
Mike: Good triage. Follow-up: schedule a retro with DNS provider re: purge SLA and consider lowering default TTL for edge-critical records.
Jin: Adding a short KB for support on how to ask customers to flush corporate resolver caches and to test EDNS behavior.
Tara: Closing temporary incident. Will link postmortem doc here when ready. support-bot: Incident INC-7531 status -> mitigated.
